title: Finite type is preserved by affine module correspondence
statement: Let $u:U\to X$ be an affine morphism [pqf-def-affine-morphism] of schemes [def-pc-scheme], and let $\mathcal A=u_*\mathcal O_U$ [def-pc-module-pullback], the sheaf of rings on $X$ with $\mathcal A(W)=\mathcal O_U(u^{-1}W)$. Let $\mathcal M$ be a sheaf of $\mathcal A$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] which is quasi-coherent as an $\mathcal A$-module (every point of $X$ has an open neighbourhood $W$ with an exact sequence $\bigoplus_{j\in J}\mathcal A|_W\to\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathcal A|_W\to\mathcal M|_W\to0$ of $\mathcal A|_W$-modules), and let $\mathcal F$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_U$-module [pqf-def-coherent] together with an isomorphism of $\mathcal A$-modules $u_*\mathcal F\cong\mathcal M$, where $u_*\mathcal F$, $W\mapsto\mathcal F(u^{-1}W)$, is an $\mathcal A$-module through the $\mathcal O_U(u^{-1}W)$-module structures (such an $\mathcal F$ exists and is unique up to isomorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-module-correspondence]). Then $\mathcal M$ is of finite type as an $\mathcal A$-module if and only if $\mathcal F$ is of finite type as an $\mathcal O_U$-module [pqf-def-coherent]. Here $\mathcal M$ is *of finite type as an $\mathcal A$-module* if it is of finite type [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation](1) over the ringed space $(X,\mathcal A)$: every point of $X$ has an open neighbourhood $W$ and finitely many sections $s_1,\dots,s_n\in\mathcal M(W)$ such that the $\mathcal A|_W$-linear map $\mathcal A|_W^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal M|_W$, $(f_1,\dots,f_n)\mapsto\sum_if_is_i$, is surjective as a map of sheaves.

proof.text: *Step 1 (setup and reformulation).* For an open $W\subseteq X$ write $W_U=u^{-1}(W)$, so $\mathcal A(W)=\mathcal O_U(W_U)$ and $(u_*\mathcal F)(W)=\mathcal F(W_U)$, with the $\mathcal O_U(W_U)=\mathcal A(W)$-module structure and the restriction maps of $\mathcal F$ (the direct image of [def-pc-module-pullback]). The given isomorphism of $\mathcal A$-modules $\theta:u_*\mathcal F\cong\mathcal M$ ([lem-weil-pbc-affine-module-correspondence] for its existence) carries sections generating as below to sections generating, in both directions, so $\mathcal M$ is of finite type over $\mathcal A$ iff $u_*\mathcal F$ is; from now on $\mathcal M=u_*\mathcal F$, $\mathcal M(W)=\mathcal F(W_U)$. For an open $W$ and $s_1,\dots,s_n\in\mathcal M(W)$ let $\sigma_s:\mathcal A|_W^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal M|_W$, $(f_i)\mapsto\sum_if_is_i|$. An $\mathcal A|_W$-linear map is an epimorphism in $\Mod(\mathcal A|_W)$ iff it is surjective as a map of sheaves, since the cokernel is the sheafification of the sectionwise cokernel [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], which is zero iff every local section is locally in the image. So $\sigma_s$ is an epimorphism iff for every open $W'\subseteq W$ and $t\in\mathcal M(W')$ there is an open covering $W'=\bigcup_kW'_k$ with $t|_{W'_k}=\sum_if_{ik}s_i|_{W'_k}$, $f_{ik}\in\mathcal A(W'_k)$; we then say that the $s_i$ *generate $\mathcal M|_W$ over $\mathcal A|_W$*. By [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation](1) for the ringed space $(X,\mathcal A)$, $\mathcal M$ is of finite type over $\mathcal A$ iff every point of $X$ has an open neighbourhood $W$ with finitely many sections of $\mathcal M(W)$ generating $\mathcal M|_W$ over $\mathcal A|_W$. If the $s_i$ generate $\mathcal M|_W$ over $\mathcal A|_W$ and $W_1\subseteq W$ is open, the restrictions $s_i|_{W_1}$ generate $\mathcal M|_{W_1}$ over $\mathcal A|_{W_1}$ (an open $W'\subseteq W_1$ is an open of $W$). Finally, for an affine open $V\subseteq X$ the open $V_U$ is affine because $u$ is affine [pqf-def-affine-morphism]; put $B=\mathcal A(V)=\mathcal O_U(V_U)$. Every point of an open $W\subseteq X$ lies in an affine open $V\subseteq W$, the open subscheme $W$ being a scheme [def-pc-scheme].

proof.text: *Step 2 (generation over $\mathcal A$ on an affine open gives generation of the sections).* Let $V\subseteq X$ be an affine open, $B$ as in Step 1, and $s_1,\dots,s_n\in\mathcal M(V)=\mathcal F(V_U)$ generating $\mathcal M|_V$ over $\mathcal A|_V$. Then $\mathcal F(V_U)=\sum_iBs_i$. Proof: $V_U$ is an affine scheme; $\mathcal F|_{V_U}$ is quasi-coherent [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits](2); and, transported along $V_U\cong\operatorname{Spec}B$, $\mathcal O_{V_U}^{\oplus n}$ is quasi-coherent with $\Gamma(V_U,\mathcal O_{V_U}^{\oplus n})=B^n$, the basis sections being the standard basis [lem-weil-pbc-spec-tilde-free-module]. Let $\psi:\mathcal O_{V_U}^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal F|_{V_U}$, $(g_i)\mapsto\sum_ig_is_i|$, an $\mathcal O_{V_U}$-linear map of quasi-coherent modules with $\psi_{V_U}(B^n)=\sum_iBs_i$. Let $t\in\mathcal F(V_U)=\mathcal M(V)$. By generation there is an open covering $V=\bigcup_kV_k$ with $t|_{V_k}=\sum_if_{ik}s_i|_{V_k}$ and $f_{ik}\in\mathcal A(V_k)=\mathcal O_U((V_k)_U)$; read in $\mathcal F$ this says $t|_{(V_k)_U}=\psi_{(V_k)_U}((f_{ik})_i)$, and the opens $(V_k)_U$ cover $V_U$. So $t$ is locally in the image of $\psi$, i.e. $t\in(\operatorname{Im}\psi)(V_U)$, and by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image](3) (for the scheme $V_U$ and its affine open $V_U$) $(\operatorname{Im}\psi)(V_U)=\psi_{V_U}(B^n)=\sum_iBs_i$.

proof.text: *Step 3 (generation of $\mathcal F$ on $V_U$ gives generation over $\mathcal A$ on $V$).* Let $V\subseteq X$ be an affine open and $s_1,\dots,s_n\in\mathcal M(V)=\mathcal F(V_U)$ sections which generate the $\mathcal O_{V_U}$-module $\mathcal F|_{V_U}$ [def-weil-pbc-generating-sections] (on the scheme $V_U$). Then the $s_i$ generate $\mathcal M|_V$ over $\mathcal A|_V$. Proof: with $\psi$ as in Step 2, the hypothesis says that $\psi$ is surjective as a map of sheaves, i.e. $\operatorname{Im}\psi=\mathcal F|_{V_U}$. Let $W\subseteq V$ be open and $t\in\mathcal M(W)=\mathcal F(W_U)$. Every $x\in W$ lies in an affine open $V'\subseteq W$ (Step 1, [def-pc-scheme]), and $V'_U$ is an affine open of the scheme $V_U$ since $u$ is affine [pqf-def-affine-morphism]. By [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image](3) for the scheme $V_U$ and its affine open $V'_U$, $\mathcal F(V'_U)=(\operatorname{Im}\psi)(V'_U)=\psi_{V'_U}(\mathcal O_U(V'_U)^n)$, so $t|_{V'_U}=\sum_if_is_i|_{V'_U}$ with $f_i\in\mathcal O_U(V'_U)=\mathcal A(V')$, which is the equation $t|_{V'}=\sum_if_is_i|_{V'}$ in $\mathcal M(V')$. These $V'$ cover $W$, so the $s_i$ generate $\mathcal M|_V$ over $\mathcal A|_V$ (Step 1).

proof.text: *Step 4 ($\mathcal M$ of finite type over $\mathcal A$ implies $\mathcal F$ of finite type).* Let $y\in U$ and $x=u(y)$. Choose an open $W\ni x$ and $s_1,\dots,s_n\in\mathcal M(W)$ generating $\mathcal M|_W$ over $\mathcal A|_W$, and an affine open $V$ with $x\in V\subseteq W$; the restrictions $s_i|_V$ generate $\mathcal M|_V$ over $\mathcal A|_V$ (Step 1). By Step 2, $\mathcal F(V_U)=\sum_iB\,s_i|_V$ is a finitely generated $B$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], with $B=\mathcal O_U(V_U)$ and $V_U$ an affine open of $U$ containing $y$. As $\mathcal F$ is quasi-coherent, [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine](a) (for the scheme $U$ and its affine open $V_U$) gives that $\mathcal F|_{V_U}$ is of finite type, so $y$ has an open neighbourhood $V''\subseteq V_U$ with a surjection $\mathcal O_{V''}^{\oplus m}\to\mathcal F|_{V''}$, which is the condition of [pqf-def-coherent] for $\mathcal F$ at $y$. As $y$ was arbitrary, $\mathcal F$ is of finite type.

proof.text: *Step 5 ($\mathcal F$ of finite type implies $\mathcal M$ of finite type over $\mathcal A$).* Let $x\in X$ and $V\ni x$ an affine open (Step 1). Since $\mathcal F$ is quasi-coherent of finite type and $V_U$ is an affine open of $U$, [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine](c) gives that $\mathcal F(V_U)$ is a finitely generated $B$-module; choose generators $s_1,\dots,s_n$. The $\mathcal O_{V_U}$-module $\mathcal F|_{V_U}$ is quasi-coherent [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits](2) and of finite type (the restriction of a surjection $\mathcal O_{W''}^{\oplus m}\to\mathcal F|_{W''}$ to $W''\cap V_U$ is still surjective as a map of sheaves), so by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-finite-type-generating-sections] (for the affine scheme $V_U$) the family $s_1,\dots,s_n$, which generates $\Gamma(V_U,\mathcal F)=\mathcal F(V_U)$, generates $\mathcal F|_{V_U}$. By Step 3 the sections $s_i\in\mathcal M(V)$ generate $\mathcal M|_V$ over $\mathcal A|_V$. As $x$ was arbitrary, $\mathcal M$ is of finite type over $\mathcal A$ by the reformulation of Step 1.
